paper_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the optimal concentration of the DIO additive differ between thin-film and thick-film PM6:IT-4F organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimal concentration of DIO additive is higher for thick-film devices (~300 nm) than for thin-film devices (~110 nm). Specifically, PM6:IT-4F thick-film devices reach peak performance at 0.6% DIO, whereas thin-film devices are optimized at a lower concentration of 0.3% DIO.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the impact of increasing DIO concentration from 0.3% to 0.6% on the recombination mechanisms within thick-film organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: Increasing the DIO content from 0.3% to 0.6% reduces both trap-assisted and bimolecular recombination. The trap-assisted recombination coefficient (s) decreases from 1.65 kT/q to 1.42 kT/q, and the bimolecular recombination exponent (alpha) increases from 0.922 to 0.959, indicating suppressed recombination losses.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: According to TOF-SIMS analysis, how does 0.6% DIO content influence the vertical component distribution in PM6:IT-4F films?
qa_pairs.answer: The 0.6% DIO content enhances the vertical component distribution by enriching the IT-4F acceptor at the surface (indicated by stronger CN- signals) and enriching the PM6 donor near the substrate (indicated by weaker CN- signals) compared to films with 0.3% DIO.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Compare the carrier lifetime and charge extraction efficiency of 0.6% DIO versus 0.3% DIO thick-film devices based on transient measurements.
qa_pairs.answer: Thick-film devices with 0.6% DIO exhibit a longer carrier lifetime of 1.95 µs compared to 1.62 µs for 0.3% DIO devices (measured by TPV). Additionally, 0.6% DIO devices show faster photocurrent decay in TPC measurements, suggesting more effective charge extraction.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What power conversion efficiencies were achieved for large-area (1 cm²) thick-film organic solar cells fabricated via blade coating in an ambient environment?
qa_pairs.answer: Large-area thick-film organic solar cells achieved a PCE of 13.94% on rigid substrates and 13.05% on flexible PET/ITO substrates.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the crystallinity of PM6 change relative to the vertical position within the active layer of a thick-film device?
qa_pairs.answer: Based on angle-dependent GIWAXS analysis, the crystallinity of PM6 (represented by the scattering intensity of the (010) π–π stacking peak) gradually increases from the top surface toward the bottom of the active layer near the substrate.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the relationship between DIO additive content and the π-π interplanar distance (d) and Crystal Coherence Length (CCL) in PM6:IT-4F blend films?
qa_pairs.answer: As the DIO content increases from 0% to 0.9%, the π-π interplanar distance (d) decreases from 3.73 Å to 3.67 Å, while the Crystal Coherence Length (CCL) increases from 1.52 nm to 1.64 nm, indicating improved molecular packing and crystallinity.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the thermal stability of PM6:Y6 thick-film devices with 0.6% CN compare to thin-film devices with 0.3% CN after 128 hours at 100 °C?
qa_pairs.answer: Both devices show similar thermal degradation: thick-film devices with 0.6% CN retain 63% of their initial PCE, while thin-film devices with 0.3% CN retain a slightly higher 68% of their initial PCE after 128 hours of heating.
qa_pairs.source_title: Modulation of Vertical Component Distribution for Large-Area Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells
